data_compute: First, use the shell tool to list `/testbed/data` and capture the exact filename (including extension) before invoking the excel tool; then open that file with the excel action, read the required range, compute the result, and write it to the specified cell reference (e.g., bottom row, new header column). Always verify the file path, sheet name, and cell coordinates match the target workbook, and avoid malformed actions by adhering strictly to the required `list`, `read`, `set_cell`, or `add_column` schemas. Before finishing, confirm that (1) the original workbook is saved with the updated data, (2) any newly created auxiliary files (e.g., a summary CSV) are written to `/testbed/data`, and (3) no temporary files remain.
multi_app: Start by invoking the shell to list /testbed/data, verify the exact filenames and paths, then switch to the source app (excel, pdf, email, etc.) and read the required data using precise parameters (sheet name, cell range, email query, etc.). Immediately after reading, switch to the target app (word, excel, etc.), create each output file with the exact filename under /testbed/data, and write the retrieved content using the correct write‑action fields. Before finishing, check that every expected output file (e.g., shopping_list.docx, result.docx, etc.) exists, that no malformed JSON or missing fields were sent, and that all file paths, names, and cell references exactly match the task specification.
single_action: Always begin by running a shell `run` command to list `/testbed/data` and verify the exact filename and path you will use. Then invoke the target app (excel, calendar, etc.) with the precise action name and payload fields—include full file paths, exact cell references or row numbers, and correct timestamps—ensuring no misspelled actions or omitted parameters. Finally, validate that every expected output (modified or copied Excel file, new calendar event, etc.) exists and is correct before signaling task completion.
lookup: First, switch to the required app (email, shell, or excel); if a file is needed, use the shell agent to list /testbed/data, capture the exact filename (including extension) and then open it with the excel agent. Next, list the relevant items (emails or files), read each target using the read action with precise identifiers (email address, subject line, or cell range such as A1:B100), and extract the requested value. Avoid malformed actions by supplying a JSON object that matches the schema, using case‑sensitive full paths, and confirming the read action returns data; before finishing, output (a) the extracted answer, (b) the name of the file or email consulted, and (c) a brief log of the actions performed.
doc_process: First, switch to the required applications in this order: use the shell agent to list and verify source files under /testbed/data, then switch to the source app (PDF, calendar, email, etc.) to retrieve the data, and finally switch to the target app (Excel, Word, etc.) to create the output, always specifying absolute paths and exact filenames; confirm each file exists before proceeding. Second, provide all parameters precisely—full /testbed/data paths, exact filenames, and for spreadsheet actions include explicit sheet names and cell references (e.g., Sheet1!A1)—to avoid malformed action calls. Third, before issuing finish_task, check that every declared output file (list each expected filename and location) has been successfully created and that no errors such as missing parameters, incorrect paths, or omitted actions remain.
